title: Number of Ways to Rearrange Sticks With K Sticks Visible
summary: Given n uniquely-sized sticks numbered 1 to n, determine the number of arrangements where exactly k sticks are visible from the left.
statement: Given n uniquely-sized sticks numbered 1 to n, determine the number of arrangements where exactly k sticks are visible from the left. A stick is visible if no longer sticks are to its left. The result should be modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Stick lengths are the distinct integers from 1 through n.
A stick is visible from the left only if every earlier stick is shorter.
reference_solution:
def count_visible_stick_arrangements(n, k):
    modulus = 1_000_000_007
    previous = [0] * (k + 1)
    previous[0] = 1
    for sticks in range(1, n + 1):
        current = [0] * (k + 1)
        for visible in range(1, min(sticks, k) + 1):
            current[visible] = (previous[visible - 1] +
                                previous[visible] * (sticks - 1)) % modulus
        previous = current
    return previous[k]

hints: Build arrangements by inserting the shortest new stick into a smaller arrangement.
Putting it first adds one visible stick; any of the other i-1 positions leaves visibility unchanged.
Use dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + (i-1)*dp[i-1][j], retaining only the previous row.
The two insertion cases are disjoint and cover every permutation exactly once, which proves the recurrence.
